job.style: a diary entry or letter by a student

response.passage: Dear Diary, today in Geography class, we learned fascinating facts about our oceans. I used to think that waves carried water all the way from the middle of the sea to the beach, but our teacher explained that waves only move the energy through the water, while the water particles themselves move in small circles. We also discussed why the ocean is salty. It is not because of decaying sea creatures, but because rivers carry dissolved salts from rocks on land into the sea over millions of years. I was surprised to learn that the water cycle is a continuous process where water evaporates from the surface, condenses into clouds, and falls as rain; the clouds do not create new water, they only store and release what has evaporated. Finally, we looked at tides. I learned that tides are the rhythmic rise and fall of ocean water caused primarily by the gravitational pull of the moon, not by the sun pushing the water around. It is amazing how the Earth's water is constantly moving and changing form, yet the total amount of water on our planet remains the same throughout history. Understanding these natural processes makes me appreciate our blue planet so much more. I cannot wait to learn more about ocean currents tomorrow!
response.summary: The passage explains that ocean waves transmit energy rather than moving water across distances. It also clarifies that ocean saltiness comes from land minerals, the water cycle is a recycling process, and tides are caused by lunar gravity.
